items.text: Bipartisan American senators are introducing legislation that would make big tech companies like Facebook and Google disclose how much money they make using your data. Last Monday, senators Josh Hawley and Mark Warner introduced the Designing Accounting Safeguards to Help Broaden Oversight and Regulations on Data, aka the DASHBOARD Act. This bill would make companies with more than 100 million monthly users inform users what data is being collected on them and how it is being used. Users would also be given the ability to delete that data. Senator Warner said that media companies told people that their product are free which is not true. People do not pay with money but with their data. The companies would also have to make a yearly report on the total value of the user data and say with which other companies they shared the data. Senator Hawley says that tech companies sell people’s data to the highest bidder and that the bill gives people control and shows them how much these ‘free’ services really cost. Facebook and Goggle have not commented on the bill yet. Difficult words: bipartisan (of two different parties, which usually do not agree with each other), disclose (say something which was secret in the past), bill (a law for discussion in the government or parliament). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

An American senator said that Internet companies say that their products are free but that is not true. He said that people do not pay for their products with money but with their data. Another senator and he prepared a bill which deals with this problem. If the bill passes, companies will have to tell people what data they collect and how they use it. Users could also delete the data. The companies would have to make a yearly report which would say how much the user’s data is worth. The companies would also have to say if they sold the data to someone else. One of the senators says that the companies sell people’s data to the highest bidder . The bill would apply to big tech companies like Facebook and Google, which have more than 100 million monthly users. Difficult words: bill (a law for discussion in the parliament), highest bidder (the company or person who pays the most money), apply (be for). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Two American senators talk about Internet companies. They say that the companies get data about people. They can use this data. They can sell the data to other companies. People do not know what data the companies have. They do not know if the companies sell the data about them. They do not know how much somebody pays for data. The senators talk about a new law . This law is for big companies like Facebook and Google. If the law passes , these companies must tell people about the data. They must tell them what they know. They must tell them if they sell it to another company. Difficult words: data (information), law (a document which says what people can or must not do), pass (if politicians say ‘yes’ to something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On Sunday, June 23 rd , Prague’s largest anti-government protests happened since the fall of the country’s communist regime in 1989. This time around, the people did not want to overthrow the political system, but support it. The protests were against the country’s prime minister, Andrej Babiš, who is facing conflict of interest allegations and is being investigated for acting criminally to get European Union funds. A EU report says that he hid the fact that he owned a farm so that he could qualify for a subsidy meant for small businesses – but Babiš is a billionaire. The report says that he should return around $20 million in subsidies in total. The peaceful protests called for Babiš and his close ally, the Czech justice minister, to step down. The minister voted against a law enforcement request to strip Babiš’s parliamentary immunity so that he could be investigated. Difficult words: conflict of interest (a situation when a politician uses their position to get richer), allegation (saying that somebody did something wrong), subsidy (grant). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The largest anti-government protests since 1989 happened in Prague on Sunday, June 23rd. People were protesting the country’s prime minister, Andrej Babiš, and his justice minister. The people demanded that Babiš step down because of questions about a possible conflict of interest and fraud . Although Babiš is a billionaire, the EU gave him money which was supposed to help small businesses. An EU report says that he hid the fact that he had a farm so he could get the grants. The report says that he should return around $20 million in total. Difficult words: demand (strongly ask for something), c onflict of interest (a situation when a politician uses his or her job to get richer), fraud (cheating, doing something illegal). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People in the Czech Republic protest. The protests are the biggest since 1989. People are protesting the country’s prime minister. They want him to step down. The prime minister’s name is Andrej Babiš. People say that he is using his position to get richer. The EU is also investigating him. The EU writes a report . It says that Babiš gets extra money from the EU. This is not OK because the money is only for small businesses. Babiš lies to get this money. He says that he does not have a farm. He is a billionaire, so this money is not for him. The report says that he must give back $20 million. Difficult words: since (from), investigate (find out more), report (an official document). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The annual Global Trends Report from the UN Refugee Agency found that the number of displaced people increased by 2.3 million from 2017 to 2018. The total number was 70 million people, which is the highest on record. This is double the number from 10 years ago, and it means that almost 1 in every 100 people are displaced. The report says that the causes are people fleeing civil wars, violence, ethnic persecution , drought, political problems, and poverty. Forty-one million people are displaced in their own countries while 26 million people are refugees. A UN refugee commissioner said that the report shows that there is a rising trend ‘in the number of people needing safety from war, conflict and persecution’. The report came out ahead of Thursday’s World Refugee Day. Difficult words: displaced people (people who have to leave their homes because of problems there), flee (run away), ethnic persecution (when people hurt or kill another group of people because they are different). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A report by a refugee agency says that the number of people who had to leave their homes increased by 2.3 million from 2017 to 2018. The total number was 70 million people. It is the highest on record and double the number from 10 years ago. The report says that people are running away from civil wars and other conflicts, droughts , political problems, and poverty . A UN leader said that the report shows that there is a rising number of people who need safety. The report came out ahead of Thursday’s World Refugee Day. Difficult words: refugee (a person who must leave their home because it is not safe), drought (when it is very dry and plants cannot grow to make food), poverty (being very poor). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A new report comes out. It is about refugees . The report says that more people leave their homes from 2017 to 2018. The total number of people is 70 million. That is the highest on record . Forty-one million people need help in their countries. Twenty-six million people are refugees. The report says that people are seeking asylum for many reasons. There is war and fighting, very dry weather, political problems, or the people do not have any money. Difficult words: refugee (a person who must leave their home because it is not safe), on record (that people know about), seek asylum (look for a safe place). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Pew Research Centre wrote its own report on the UN’s World Populations Prospects for 2019, in which the UN estimates that the world population will grow from 7.7 billion now to 10.9 billion in 2100. The reports say that five African countries will add over half of that population increase by 2050 and one Asian country will add over half of that increase in 2100. Pew also says that the yearly population growth rate will fall from 1–2% a year to 0.1%. One reason is the average fertility rate will fall. One woman has 2.5 births a year now, but it will fall to 1.9 births in 2100. The UN says that based on this data, is possible that the world’s population will increase, stabilise , or decrease. Difficult words: prospects (chances, potentials), fertility rate (how many children you can have), stabilise (stop getting bigger or smaller). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The UN wrote a report about the global population. It estimates that the population will grow from 7.7 billion now to 10.9 billion in 2100. The Pew Research Centre looked at this report and wrote its own report. Five African countries in 2050 and one Asian country in 2100 will have the biggest population growth. Pew also said that while there is going to be more people, the growth rate will fall because the average fertility rate will fall. The UN said that based on its report, the world’s population will grow, get smaller, or stop changing. Difficult words: estimate (predict, guess with data), growth rate (how fast something grows), average fertility rate (the number of children most women have). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The UN writes a report about the number of people in the world. The UN believes that the population will grow. There are 7.7 billion people in the world right now. There will be 10.9 billion people the world in 2100. The Pew Research Centre looks at this report. It writes its own report. Both reports say that countries in Africa and Asia will grow the most. However, Pew says that the population growth will stop. This is because women will have fewer babies. The UN says that the global population can do three things: it can grow, it can get smaller, or it can stop changing. Difficult words: will (in the future), fewer (not as may), global population (all the people in the world). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Chinese President Xi Jinping met North Korean leader Kim Jong-un in the first trip by a Chinese leader to North Korea in 14 years. The meeting was largely a symbolic show of the countries’ united front before the G-20 summit which starts tomorrow in Japan. The red carpet was rolled out and hundreds of thousands lined the streets to wave flags in a typically North Korean fashion, as the two leaders drove by, standing and waving from the car. The two leaders attended a banquet and then a gymnastics performance, titled ‘Undefeated Socialism’, where Kim said that socialism is the core of North Korean–China friendship and that the two countries must protect it and build it together. The discussion the two heads had was possibly the most important part of the trip but both countries have been vague about what they said. However, Xi said that China would continue to mediate talks between USA and North Korea. A North Korean state media outlet reported that Kim and Xi also talked about their opinions on the political situation of the Korean Peninsula and other serious international and regional issues. Difficult words: banquet (a formal meal for many people), core (the deepest, most important part), vague (unclear, not giving information). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Chinese President Xi Jinping met North Korean leader Kim Jong-un. It was the first trip by a Chinese leader to North Korea in 14 years. The meeting was mostly symbolic – it showed the friendship of the two countries before the G-20 summit. The summit starts tomorrow in Japan. The red carpet was rolled out and thousands of people waved flags along the streets. The two leaders attended a banquet and then a gymnastics performance titled ‘ Undefeated Socialism’. Kim said that socialism is the most important part of the North Korean–China friendship and that the two countries must protect it and build it together. The two leaders later had a discussion, but it is not known what they discussed. However, Xi said China would continue to mediate talks between USA and North Korea. People later said that Kim and Xi talked about the political situation in North and South Korea and other serious international and regional problems. Difficult words: banquet (a formal dinner for many people), undefeated (not defeated – not beaten), mediate (work with two groups to help them get along). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Chinese President Xi Jinping meets North Korean leader Kim Jong-un. Xi travels to North Korea. This is the first time that a Chinese president travels there in 14 years. In North Korea, Xi Jinping gets a great welcome. There is a red carpet. People wave flags along the streets. The two leaders have dinner. They watch a gymnastics performance. Kim says that socialism is the most important things for North Korea and China. He says that China and North Korea must protect it. They must build it together. Kim and Xi talk. We do not know much of what they talk about. However, the meeting is mostly symbolic. North Korea and China want to show that they are friends. They do this before the G-20 summit . It starts tomorrow in Japan. Difficult words: flag (a country’s official symbol), socialism (a style of managing a country, the economy and people), G-20 summit (a meeting of leaders of 20 important countries). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Someone shot down the Malaysian Airlines Flight 17 over eastern Ukraine in 2014. All 298 people on board died. Now, international investigators charged four men with murder of the people. Police issued national and international arrest warrants for one Ukrainian and three Russian nationals last Wednesday. The criminal trial is set to begin in March 2020. The investigators say that they will move forward with the trial even if the suspects are not present, which will likely be the case. The prosecutors also say that they will not ask for extradition , since Ukraine and Russia do not extradite nationals. Difficult words: arrest warrant (a document from a lawyer or a country which says that police can arrest somebody), prosecutors (the people who take legal action against somebody), extradition (the act of extraditing somebody – giving a criminal to another country’s court). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In 2014, someone shot down the Malaysian Airlines Flight 17 over eastern Ukraine. All 298 people on board died. Now, international investigators charged four men with murder of the people. One is from Ukraine and three are from Russia. The trial is set to begin in March 2020. Difficult words: investigator (a person who investigates a crime – finds out what happened and who did it), charge (formally say that somebody did something illegal), trial (a situation at court when lawyers decide if somebody is guilty – goes to prison, or is set free). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Somebody shoots down an airplane in Ukraine. This is in 2014. There are 298 people on the plane. All of them die. In 2014, people do not know who shoots down the plane. Now, investigators find the criminals. They know their names. One of them is from Ukraine. Three are from Russia. The trial is going to be in March 2020. Difficult words: shoot (use a gun), investigator (a person who finds criminals), trial (a situation at court when lawyers say if somebody goes to prison or is set free). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Last Tuesday, Facebook unveiled its plans for its digital currency project and a cryptocurrency called Libra. An independent non-profit called the Libra Association will run the digital currency, and it has the backing of some big corporate partners, including Mastercard, PayPal and Uber. The service is currently in the testing phase but when it launches in 2020, users will be able to send Libra to each other using Facebook’s services like Messenger, WhatsApp or its upcoming digital wallet, Calibra. Other apps will also be able to integrate Libra. Libra transactions are recorded on a blockchain, which is the same technology that bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies use. Facebook says that its goal is to make it easy to transfer money globally without the fees that are incurred in a traditional banking infrastructure. When it comes to converting Libra into actual cash, though, users may run into the same issues as other cryptocurrencies – not all places accept it and not all financial institutions want to trade it for traditional money. When it comes to privacy, some are also concerned with Facebook’s reputation. The company stated that in most cases, users’ financial and account information will not be shared with Facebook or third parties without consent. Some US politicians called on Facebook to stop the cryptocurrency project until federal regulators and lawmakers have a chance to weigh in . Difficult words: unveil (show people for the first time), launch (start), weigh in (contribute in the discussion, say something about it). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last Tuesday, Facebook talked about its plans for its digital currency project called Libra. An independent company called the Libra Association will run the digital currency. The project also has help from big partners including Mastercard, PayPal and Uber. People are testing the Libra service and it will be available in 2020. Users will be able to send Libra to each other using Facebook’s services like Messenger, WhatsApp or its upcoming digital wallet, Calibra. Other apps will also be able to use Libra. The cryptocurrency uses the same technology as bitcoin. Facebook wants to make it easy to transfer money around the world for free. However, not all business may accept Libra and not all financial institutions may want to trade it for traditional money. Some people are also concerned about privacy – Facebook does not have a very good reputation. Facebook says that your information will not be shared with them in most cases. Difficult words: currency (money), independent (free, not part of another company), concerned (worried). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Facebook talks about its plans. It is working on a digital currency . The currency is called Libra. The project has help from big partners like Mastercard, PayPal and Uber. People can use Libra in 2020. They can send Libra in Messenger and WhatsApp. There will be a new app, too. It is called Calibra. It will be a digital Libra wallet. Other apps can use Libra, too. Libra is similar to bitcoin. Facebook is doing this so people can send money around the world for free. However, some people do not trust Facebook. For example, some people worry that Facebook can look at how much Libra they have. Difficult words: currency (money), will (in the future), trust (if you trust somebody, you know that he or she is good). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People restored Internet and text messaging services like WhatsApp and Telegram in Ethiopia last Tuesday after the country was offline for a week. The country’s mobile service provider told CNN that the company would credit customers for services that were affected during the web blackout . The country’s economy also hurt from the outage – people say that the country lost around $17 million. This was another time that the Internet has been shut off in Ethiopia – in 2018, people turned it off for months in areas that had unrest. It is not clear what caused the shut down, but some people think that this one occurred to prevent students from cheating on national exams. Difficult words: blackout (the time when a service is down), occur (happen), prevent (keep from doing something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The Internet was down for a week in Ethiopia and people restored it last Tuesday. The country’s service provider said that it would credit people who did not have Internet. It also said that the state lost around $17 million. People do not known why the Internet went down. Some think that someone turned it off to stop students from cheating on national exams. This also has happened before. In 2018, there was no Internet for months in areas of Ethiopia where people were protesting. Difficult words: restore (make something work again), provider (a company which provides – sells the Internet), credit (give money or something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is about the Internet in Ethiopia. There are protests in some areas in Ethiopia in 2018. The Internet is off in these areas. Last week, the Internet is off again. It is down for a week. People do not know why. Some people think that it is because of students. They think that no Internet can stop students from cheating . The country’s Internet provider says that it is going to give money to people. The country loses money in the outage , too. People say that Ethiopia loses around $17 million. Difficult words: cheat (do not do what you are supposed to do; for example, do not study but look at someone else’s exam to do well on an exam), provider (a company/business which sells or provides the Internet), outage (a time when there is no Internet). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The failure of two Argentine hydroelectric plants led to a system-wide meltdown that affected nearly 50 million people in Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay. The hydroelectric dams went down at 7 a.m. local time last Sunday and the lights were mostly back at night, but Argentine officials said that the outage should have been only a localised event. Argentine President Mauricio Macri said that it will be carefully investigated why the system-wide meltdown happened. The total blackout also happened when some Argentine provinces were holding gubernatorial elections – people had to vote by the light of their cell phones. Difficult words: meltdown (collapse), outage (when there is no service, like electricity), gubernatorial (about the future governor). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last Sunday morning, two hydroelectric plants in Argentina failed, and this did not lead to a localised power outage but to a massive blackout . Nearly 50 million people in Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay were affected because the whole system broke down. The Argentine president said that people are going to carefully investigate the incident. The blackout happened when people were voting for governors in some Argentine provinces – people had to use their phones as lights to vote. Difficult words: hydroelectric plant (a big wall which holds water – some water goes down and makes electricity), outage (when there is no service, such as electricity), blackout (an electricity outage). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Last Sunday, two hydroelectric plants in Argentina fail. This happens in the morning. This makes the whole system fail. Almost 50 million people lose electricity. Most of them are in Argentina. Uruguay and Paraguay also lose power. People want to know why the system fails. They are investigating the incident. Difficult words: hydroelectric plant (a big wall which holds water – some water goes down and makes electricity), whole system (the complete group), investigate (find out why something happens). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

According to state-run media, the former Egyptian president, Mohammed Morsi, died shortly after a court appearance last Monday. He was attending a hearing for his trial in an espionage lawsuit when he collapsed and died before he could go to hospital. He had been serving prison sentences for various crimes, and people say that his imprisonment conditions were contributing to his deteriorating health in recent years. He became Egypt’s first democratically elected president in 2012 after Mubarak during the Arab Spring. A year later, however, the military overthrew him, following mass anti-government protests. Other now-banned leaders from the Muslim Brotherhood and he were arrested and jailed. Difficult words: former (-ex), espionage (being a spy), deteriorate (get worse). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In 2012, Mohammed Morsi was Egyptian first democratically elected president. A year later, however, the military overthrew him, following mass anti-government protests. Other leaders from the Muslim Brotherhood and he were arrested and jailed. People say that because of bad conditions in that jail, his health got worse in recent years. According to state-run media, he was at court last Monday, collapsed and died before he could go to hospital. Difficult words: elect (vote for, choose), collapse (fall down suddenly). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In 2012, Mohammed Morsi becomes the Egyptian President. He is president for one year. Many people protest. The army overthrows him. He goes to jail. People say that the jail’s conditions are bad. He gets sick. Last Monday, he is at court . He falls down and he dies. Difficult words: overthrow (bring down from power), condition (how a place is; for example, how clean the jail is), court (an institution which finds out if you are guilty or innocent). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In May, the EU held elections to the European Parliament, and the most people came to vote since 1994. Many people voted for parties that favour countries’ independent rights, but most people still voted for pro-EU politicians. Now, the EU says that it has evidence that Russian groups tried to influence those elections. The EU’s report found disinformation activity from Russia that tried to suppress people from voting, change their views, or polarise people. The report said that some social media companies tried to help fight the disinformation, but ‘more needs to be done to protect’ the processes. The report did not blame the Russian government directly, neither did it say if the disinformation actually changed how people voted. Difficult words: disinformation (fake information that looks like real information), suppress (stop, slow down), polarise (turn people into groups through extreme views). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In May, the EU had elections to the European Parliament. Now the EU says that it has evidence that Russian groups tried to influence those elections. The EU’s report said that Russians tried to stop people from going to vote, tried to change how they were going to vote, or tried to make them angry. The report said that social media companies helped with this problem but that more needs to be done. The report did not blame the Russian government directly or say if the tactics actually changed how people voted. Difficult words: evidence (things which show that something really happened), influence (make changes), tactic (an action, an attempt to do something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In May, the EU holds elections to the European Parliament. Now the EU has a report. The report says that Russian groups try to change the elections. The report says that the Russians do this in a few ways. They do not want a high voter turnout . They want to change how people vote. They want people to be angry. The report says that social media companies help. However, more work needs to be done. The report does not blame Russian leaders. It does not say if the elections are changed. Difficult words: election (when people choose their leaders), voter turnout (how many people go to the election), blame (say that someone did something on purpose). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

‘Deepfakes’ are a new type of manipulated content. For example, people can use technology to change how a video looks or how audio sounds, and it is also difficult for people to tell that it is fake. US politicians are concerned because they say that ‘ malicious actors’ can use deepfakes to create problems for elections and disrupt campaigns in the 2020 elections. The issue is difficult to control because of the ubiquity of social media, and the speeds at which information spreads on the Internet. Some people feel that if deepfakes are defamatory , they should be removed. Others say that removing false media limits free speech. Experts asked lawmakers to work with social media companies to police this issue better. Difficult words: malicious (someone who wants to do something bad), ubiquity (when something is everywhere), defamatory (saying something negative and untrue about a person). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

People can now use technology to manipulate videos or audio to make ‘deepfakes’. It is difficult for others to tell if the new media is fake. Deepfakes worry American politicians because they say that people can use them to disrupt the election process in the 2020 elections. This problem is difficult to control because social media is everywhere, and information spreads quickly on the Internet. Some people say that businesses should take deepfakes down if they are harmful to a person’s reputation. Others say that doing this limits free speech . Difficult words: manipulate (change something into something similar or new), disrupt (break up, upset), free speech (the right to say or write what you think). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People use technology to change videos or audio. Sometimes other people cannot tell that the new videos or audio are not real. These new things are called ‘deepfakes’. Deepfakes worry American leaders. They think that people can use them to disrupt the election process in 2020. It is very hard to stop deepfakes. They are on social media. Social media are everywhere. Also, information moves quickly on the Internet. Deepfakes can hurt a person’s reputation . Some people think that businesses should take deepfakes down. Other people say that people can say what they want. Difficult words: disrupt (break up, upset, do something bad), election process (when people choose new leaders), reputation (what people think about you). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Nearly two years after the Grenfell Tower fire in London, survivors and families of those who died are taking legal action against three companies over the catastrophe in which 72 people died. The lawsuit filed in the USA last Tuesday says that a Whirlpool refrigerator was responsible for starting the fire, while Arconic cladding and Celotex insulation burnt as fast as to turn the building into a ‘flaming coffin’. According to the Washington Post, all three companies said that they would work with authorities to investigate the fire. Difficult words: lawsuit (an official document which says that somebody did something illegal), cladding (the material which is on top of insulation to protect the building from weather and make it look nice), insulation (the material on a wall which keeps the building warm in winter). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The Grenfell Tower fire in London took place almost two years ago, and seventy-two people died in the catastrophe. Survivors and families of those who died are taking legal action against three companies in the USA. The lawsuit says that a Whirlpool refrigerator was responsible for starting the fire. The materials on the walls of the building were made by companies Arconic and Celotex. The document says that the problem was that the materials burned really fast. According to the Washington Post, all three companies said that they would work with authorities to investigate the fire. Difficult words: legal (official, using lawyers), lawsuit (an official document which says that somebody did something illegal), authorities (people who are in charge of somewhere, such as police). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In 2017, a building in London is on fire. It is a high building where people live. Its name is Grenfell Tower. The fire is very big. Seventy-two people die. Survivors are filing a lawsuit against three companies. The lawsuit says that a Whirlpool fridge starts the fire. Materials in the building then burn really fast. These materials are made by Arconic and Celotex. Difficult words: survivor (people who live after the fire), file (put in), lawsuit (an official document which says that somebody did something illegal/wrong/bad). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Hong Kong’s central government plans to let China request that people in Hong Kong accused of certain crimes be sent to mainland China for trial. This comes in the context of a murder case in Taiwan – the criminal ended up in Hong Kong’s court system. Hong Kong’s head of government wants to put a stop to this, so that criminals cannot take refuge in the city. However, pro-democracy activists fear that the new extradition law is another example of China trying to control Hong Kong. People filled the streets to show that they are against the law. Although Hong Kong is a Chinese city, it is different from the rest of China because it was a British colony. In 1997, Britain handed the territory back under a special agreement with China known as ‘one country, two system’. Hong Kong’s autonomy is supposed to last until 2047, but China has signalled that it might not be willing to wait that long. Difficult words: accused (a person officially in trouble because they maybe did something illegal), take refuge (go somewhere safe), extradition (handing over an accused person to a foreign country). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Hong Kong was a British colony which Britain gave back to China in 1997. However, the city is autonomous and its autonomy from China should last until 2047. However, China sometimes signals that it will not wait so long. Many people in Hong Kong are afraid that China is trying to get more power from Hong Kong. There are protests in Hong Kong at the moment over an extradition law. This law would let China take criminals accused of some crimes in Hong Kong. The head of Hong Kong’s government says that it is a good law because criminals can be safe in Hong Kong without the law, but people are afraid that China is trying to get more power from this. Difficult words: autonomous (free), extradition (giving an accused person to a foreign country), accused (a person officially in trouble because they maybe did something illegal). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Hong Kong is in China. It is different from China. Hong Kong was British. Now, it is free from China. It is going to be free from China until 2047. However, China wants Hong Kong. It wants more power. It shows that it wants Hong Kong sooner than 2047. Some Hongkongers do not like this. They do not want to be part of China. Now there are protests in Hong Kong. People protest because of a new law . If this law passes , China can take some criminals from courts in Hong Kong and put them in a Chinese court. Difficult words: was (past of ‘is’), law (a document which says what people can and cannot/must not do), pass (happen, start to be real for people), court (an institution which says if a criminal goes to jail or goes home). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Russia is definitely not the safest country for journalists – people say that 58 reporters have been killed in the country since 1992. Most recently, Ivan Golunov, an investigative reporter for the news site Meduza, was arrested on June 6. He was known for his exposés on local government corruption in Moscow. The police said that he had drugs which he was going to sell, which could lead to up 20 years in prison, but his supporters said that the police planted the drugs. His arrest led to demonstrations which pushed Russian authorities to set the journalist free. However, the demonstrations continued until last Wednesday, ever after charges against Golunov were dropped. Police responded to the demonstrations, arresting more than 500 people, which included a leading opposition politician. On Thursday, the Kremlin got involved and fired two police major generals in Moscow and the city’s drug control chief for their roles in opening a criminal case against Golunov. Difficult words: exposé (a report which shows something bad), charge (officially saying that somebody did something illegal). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Russia is not a safe country for journalists, as people say that 58 reporters were killed there between 1992 and 2019. Most recently, Ivan Golunov, an investigative reporter for the news site Meduza, was arrested on June 6. People knew him for exposing corruption in Moscow. The police said that he had drugs which he was going to sell. He was facing up to 20 years in prison, but his supporters said that the police planted the drugs. The supporters also started demonstrating which pushed the police to let Golunov go and set him free of any trouble. However, the demonstrations went on. The police arrested more than 500 people. The Kremlin was involved on Thursday and fired three police generals for their roles in opening a criminal case against Golunov. Difficult words: expose (show), supporter (somebody who supports – likes and helps someone), plant (secretly put something to get a person in trouble). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Russia is not safe for journalists. Between 1992 and 2019, 58 reporters are killed in Russia. Ivan Golunov is a Russian reporter. People know him because he shows corruption in Moscow. Golunov is not killed but police arrest him. Police say that they find drugs. Golunov’s supporters say that the drugs are not his. They say that the police put the drugs in his things. Some people in Moscow start to protest. Police let Golunov go. He is free. He is not in any trouble. However, people are still protesting. The Kremlin gets involved . Three police generals lose their jobs. Difficult words: corruption (bad things which politicians do), supporter (somebody who supports – likes and helps someone), get involved (start doing something about a situation). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Vatican released a 31-page paper which explains in detail how Catholic schools, parents and others should talk about ‘gender theory’. The document says that ‘radical’ forms of gender identity are based on ‘nothing more than a confused concept of freedom in the [area] of feelings and wants’. The paper goes on to say that the idea of being transgender or gender neutral is not real. Some LGBTQ groups were quick to criticise the Vatican, as they see the matter differently. People wrote the document in February 2019 but they released it now in June, which is Pride Month. Such timing also raised some questions. People chose june to be the LGBT Pride Month to remember the Stonewall rebellion, which took place at the end of June 1969. The rebellion was a demonstration against police attacks on people in a gay bar in New York. It is important to say, though, that the document also calls for respect for everyone. It says: ’No one should suffer bullying , violence , insults or unjust discrimination based on their specific characteristics.’ Difficult words: bully (do bad things to somebody), violence (being violent – attacking somebody), insult (saying something which makes another person feel very bad). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The Vatican released a 31-page paper that explains in detail how Catholic schools, parents and others should talk about ‘gender theory’. The document criticises ‘radical’ forms of gender identity. It says that gender identity is based on only feeling, wants and confusion . The paper goes on to say that the idea of being transgender or gender neutral is not real. Some LGBTQ groups were quick to criticise the Vatican because they see things differently. Also, some people are thinking about why the document was released in June because people wrote it in February 2019. The month of June is the Pride Month. People choose to remember the Stonewall rebellion, which took place at the end of June 1969. The rebellion was a demonstration against police attacks on people in a gay bar in New York. However, the document says that everyone should be respected. The Vatican is against attacking people or saying terrible things to them only because they are ‘different’. Difficult words: release (show to people), based on (built on), confusion (when people are confused – they think many things and they do not know what is true). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Vatican writes a document. It is 31 pages long. It talks about ‘gender theory’. It tells Catholic schools, parents and others how to talk about ‘gender theory’. The document criticises ‘radical’ forms of gender identity. It says that gender identity is only about what people feel and what they want. It says that there is some confusion . The document says that being transgender or gender neutral is not real. Some LGBTQ groups react to the document. They do not like it. However, the document also talks about respect. The Vatican thinks that everyone must be respected. People can be who they want to be. It is important to respect them. It is not OK to attack people. It is not OK to say terrible things to them. Difficult words: confusion (when people are confused – they think many things and they do not know what is true), terrible (very bad). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section. Question: What do you think about this news?

Last Monday in New York, a helicopter crashed about 11 minutes after take-off when it hit the roof of a 51-storey skyscraper. Only the pilot died in the crash, and no one else was injured. People are investigating the incident, but Mayor Bill de Blasio said that there is no indication that the crash was an act of terrorism and that there is no ongoing threat to New York City. The crash started a fire, but people managed to put it out quickly. A large part of mid-town Manhattan including Times Square had to temporarily close. Difficult words: indication (a sign, a piece of information), threat (danger), temporarily (for a limited time). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last Monday, a helicopter in New York crashed on the roof of a skyscraper. The crash happened about 11 minutes after take-off. Only the pilot was in the helicopter when it crashed. He died, but no one else was injured. The crash started a fire which people quickly put out . People are investigating the incident , but the Mayor of New York City said that it was not an act of terrorism. Difficult words: put out (stop something like a fire), incident (a situation). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A helicopter takes off . It crashes after 11 minutes. It crashes on the roof of a skyscraper . This happens on Monday in New York. Only the pilot is in the helicopter. He dies. The crash starts a fire. People put it out quickly. No one else is injured in the crash. Difficult words: take off (get in the air, start flying), skyscraper (a very tall building), put out (stop). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Americans have not been allowed to travel to Cuba as tourists for many years. They can only visit Cuba to see family, conduct government business or do humanitarian work. Now, the Trump Administration is making it even more difficult for Americans to travel to the Caribbean country. A type of educational travel called ‘people-to-people’ will no longer be allowed. It let Americans travel to Cuba in organised tour groups. Their itinerary only had to consist of a ‘full-time schedule’ of activities which involved contact with the local population. The US government is also going to prohibit private and corporate planes and passenger boats and ships from going to Cuba. It said that the new travel restrictions are a response to the country’s ‘destabilising role in the Western Hemisphere’, including its support of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro. Difficult words: conduct (do, carry out), itinerary (a travel plan), prohibit (make illegal). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Americans are not allowed to travel to Cuba as tourists. They can only visit Cuba to see family, do government business or do humanitarian work. The Trump Administration is making it even more difficult for Americans to travel to the Caribbean country. In the past, they could travel there under a programme called ‘people-to-people’. Under this programme, you had to meet the locals . Now the ‘people-to-people’ travelling will no longer be allowed. The American government says that it is doing this because it does not like Cuba’s foreign policy . Difficult words: allow (let somebody do something), the locals (the people who live somewhere; in this article, Cubans), foreign policy (how a country communicates with other countries and what the country does). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Americans cannot simply travel to Cuba. There are only four situations when they can. They can visit their family in Cuba. They can do government business. They can do humanitarian work . There is also a programme called ‘people-to-people’. Americans can visit with this programme. They must meet Cubans to travel with the programme. The American government stops this programme. It is harder for Americans to travel to Cuba. The American government says that it does this because it does not like Cuba’s foreign policy . Difficult words: government (the ‘bosses’ of a country), humanitarian work (helping people), foreign policy (how a country communicates with other countries and what the county does). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On May 30, President Trump said that he would put growing tariffs on Mexico’s imports if Mexico did not slow down the illegal immigration happening between the two countries. The threat of tariffs worried people in both countries. Last year, the US imported $378 billion of items from Mexico. Last week, the US and Mexico made a deal to stop President Trump’s threat to put tariffs on Mexico’s imports. After several days of negotiating, President Trump tweeted that the tariffs would be ‘ indefinitely suspended’ . As part of the deal, Mexico will increase its use of its National Guard to stop illegal immigration by adding 6,000 troops to its border. The US will continue to run its illegal immigration programmes at its border. In 90 days, the two countries will meet again to see if the deal is working well. Difficult words: tariff (a tax on sending items to another country), indefinitely (for a time without a fixed limit), suspend (stop). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

On May 30, President Trump said that he would put tariffs on Mexico’s imports because he wanted Mexico to slow down the illegal immigration to the USA. Last week, the USA and Mexico made a deal, and Trump agreed not to start the tariffs. As part of the deal, Mexico will increase its use of its National Guard by 6,000 men to stop illegal immigration. The USA will continue to work against illegal immigration at the border with Mexico, too. In 90 days, the two countries will meet again to see if the deal is working well. Difficult words: tariff (a tax on things which are sent to another country), import (things moved to a country from another country), National Guard (the army that protects a country and stays in that country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People are coming from Mexico to the USA. Some of them come illegally . Trump wants this to stop. He wants Mexico to stop them. He says that if Mexico does nothing, he puts a tax on things which Mexico sells to the USA. Last week, the USA and Mexico make a deal . Mexico is going to try to stop the people. Trump says that he will not start the tax. Difficult words: illegally (it is a crime to do it), tax (extra money that you have to pay to send something to another country), deal (a plan). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A 2017 study found that American and Canadian women were 27% less likely to receive CPR in public than men. The JOAN Creative agency thought that the statistic came because people were not trained on women’s bodies and were not sure about touching women’s breasts during CPR, so they created an attachment for flat-chested CPR dummies . The attachment is called the Womanikin, and it basically adds breasts onto the male dummy. The creator told CNN that ‘the Womanikin won’t solve everything, but it’s a step in the right direction’ and people hope to make it available for CPR classes across the USA by the end of next year. Hopefully, it will make a difference and more women who suffer cardiac arrest in public will be saved. Difficult words: CPR (short for cardiopulmonary resuscitation – massaging somebody’s heart and breathing into their mouth), attachment (an extra part), dummy (a model of a person), cardiac arrest (when someone’s heart stops beating). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A 2017 study found that American and Canadian women were 27% less likely to receive CPR in public than men. Some people thought about the reasons for this. One of the reasons could be that people are taught to perform CPR on dummies with flat chests. To solve this problem, people created the Womanikin which can add breasts on the dummies. The creators say that this is not going to make everything OK, but it was a step in the right way. They hope to have it in classes across the USA by the end of next year. Difficult words: CPR (short for cardiopulmonary resuscitation – massaging somebody’s heart and breathing into his or her mouth when the heart stops working), dummy (a model of a person), breasts (two soft organs on the front a woman’s body). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A person has a cardiac arrest when his or her heart stops working. This is very dangerous. You can help this person by giving him or her CPR. When you give CPR, you press down on the person’s chest . You massage the person’s heart like this. You breathe into the person’s mouth, too. Scientists do a study. They study how many people give CPR in public . They find out that women get 23% less CPR than men. Some people want to know why. People use models to learn CPR. The models look like men. They do not look like women. The people think that this reason can be why. They make the Womanikin. You put the Womanikin on the model. The model looks like a woman, not a man, with the Womankin. Difficult words: chest (the front part of your body between the neck and the belly), breathe (pull in or push out air), public (out with other people), find out (learn). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
